title: catch me wearing my ‘Mother’ hat forever. ✨#ashseesallthetheater #ani...
transcript: Join me at the theater tonight I'm seeing Mother Play: A Play in Five Evictions at Second Stage. Paula Vogel is one of my favorite playwrights of all time so I was extremely excited when Second Stage announced they were going to be producing a world premiere play of hers this is the first time that Paula Vogel has had a world premiere on Broadway and it's really exciting normally plays will run regionally or maybe off Broadway and then transfer this show is still in previous so it's literally actively being worked on also like the best merch on Broadway Mother Play is an autobiographical work about Paula Vogel's family it's about her mother and her brother and their complex relationships growing up The cast is unreal Celia Keenan-Bolger and Jim Parsons playing siblings Martha and Carl and Jessica Lange playing their mother Jessica Lange is absolutely incredible and the show is really funny even goofy at points and so heartfelt but also touches on a lot of really important and painful issues after the show I was on my way out and I noticed that people we’re still saying seated I had missed a slip saying there was going to be a talk back with Paula Vogel herself it was amazing hearing about how she had written the show how much was changing every single day I posted a little clip yesterday that I thought was really cool but I was just really in awe of hearing her insight how she chose to tell this immensely personal story. I very much wanted to deal with the history of class and racism and homophobia that happened in my home. The actually happened I forgave my mother she asked my forgiveness I asked for hers before she died. So insanely special. Go see Mother Play.
reasoning: The reviewer expresses strong enthusiasm throughout, praising the cast (especially Jessica Lange as 'absolutely incredible'), the writing, the humor, and the emotional depth. They end with a direct recommendation ('Go see Mother Play') and describe the experience as 'insanely special.'
